statement: Define that a label v is a judge exactly when 1 <= v <= n, there is no index i with 0 <= i < len(trust) and trust[i][0] = v, and for every label u with 1 <= u <= n and u != v there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(trust), trust[i][0] = u, and trust[i][1] = v. The function returns a result r and: if a judge exists, then r is its label (under the preconditions there is at most one such label); if no judge exists, then r = -1.
preconditions: n and every trust entry are i64 integers; 1 <= n <= 1000; 0 <= len(trust) <= 10^4; for every i with 0 <= i < len(trust), len(trust[i]) = 2, 1 <= trust[i][0] <= n, 1 <= trust[i][1] <= n, and trust[i][0] != trust[i][1]; all ordered pairs (trust[i][0], trust[i][1]) for 0 <= i < len(trust) are pairwise distinct.
